**Why it matters:** the prorated quota is the denominator of attainment, so the method decides the tier. It can also create a start-date cliff, where one day moves a quota by a full month.

**Worked scenario:** Q1 2026 runs Jan 1 – Mar 31, which is 90 days. Full quota is $90,000. The rep starts Feb 15 and books $50,000.

| Method | Prorated quota | Attainment | Earned |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Calendar days, start day inclusive (45 of 90) | **$45,000.00** | 111.1% | 5% × $45,000 + 8% × $5,000 = **$2,650.00** |
| B. Months, start month counted in full (2 of 3) | **$60,000.00** | 83.3% | 5% × $50,000 = **$2,500.00** |
| C. Whole months only, start month excluded (1 of 3) | **$30,000.00** | 166.7% | 5% × $30,000 + 8% × $15,000 + 12% × $5,000 = **$3,300.00** |

Under B and C, starting Feb 28 instead of Feb 1 changes nothing, while starting Mar 1 instead of Feb 28 moves the quota by $30,000.

**Recommended:** Option A. It's proportional to time actually employed, has no cliffs, and is exact for any start date. One detail: a non-round fraction such as 46/90 of $90,000 = $46,000.00 is fine, but 46/91 of $100,000 = $50,549.4505… needs a rounding rule. That's a separate question I'll ask.

|---|---|
| A | Calendar days: full quota × (days from start date to quarter end, both inclusive) ÷ (days in quarter). |
| B | Months, counting the start month in full. |
| C | Whole months only, excluding a partial start month. |
| D | Mid-month convention: the start month counts in full if the start is on or before the 15th, otherwise not at all. |

| Reading | Clawback | Rep keeps |
|---|---|---|
| A. Recompute the quarter without the deal. It no longer counts toward attainment, and the clawback is the difference. | $6,600 − (5% × $60,000) = **$3,600.00** | $3,000.00 |
| B. Stack deals in booking-date order and reverse the refunded deal's own slices. A sat in the first $60,000 at 5%. It still counts toward attainment. | **$3,000.00** | $3,600.00 |
| C. Rep's blended rate on the deal: $6,600 / $120,000 = 5.5% × $60,000 | **$3,300.00** | $3,300.00 |

**Recommended:** Option A. The rep ends up paid exactly as if the refunded deal had never been booked. No ordering rule is needed, and the result is the same whichever deal is refunded. The breakdown would show the pre-refund commission, then a clawback line citing FR-016 for the difference.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| A | Recompute without the refunded deal (it no longer counts toward attainment); the clawback is the difference. |
| B | Reverse the deal's own attributed slices, stacking deals in booking-date order; the deal still counts toward attainment. |
| C | The deal's credited amount × the rep's blended effective rate for the quarter. |

| C | Owed back: the shortfall is shown as an amount the rep owes. |

**Worked scenario 1 (where rounding happens):** Q2 2026 has 91 days. Full quota is $100,000. The rep starts May 16, so 46 days remain. They book $60,000.

| Reading | Prorated quota | 5% line | 8% line | Earned |

Under C, the lines shown ($2,527.47 + $756.04 = $3,283.51) don't add up to the total shown ($3,283.52).

**Worked scenario 2 (how a half-cent rounds):** a 5% slice of $10.10 is $0.505.
- Half away from zero gives **$0.51**.

**Recommended:** Option A. Every displayed line is the actual amount used downstream, so a statement always adds up and anyone can re-check it with a calculator. Half away from zero is the ordinary rounding people expect on a paycheck. Banker's rounding avoids bias only across large volumes, and it looks like an error on a single statement.

**Run 2, question 4 of 5**

**Question:** Which quarter's statement carries a clawback: the quarter the deal was booked in, or the quarter the refund happens in? (FR-016)

**Why it matters:** a refund often lands after the quarter's commission was already paid. The two readings put the clawback on different statements, and one of them can take a quarter's commission below zero.

**Worked scenario:** in Q1 the quota is $100,000 and deals A and B are $60,000 each, so Q1 earned is $6,600.00. Deal A is refunded on 2026-04-15, in Q2. In Q2 the rep books $40,000 against a $100,000 quota, earning $2,000.00, with $12,000.00 of draws and an opening balance of $0.

| Reading | Q1 earned | Q2 earned | Q2 closing recoverable balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Restate the booking quarter: the clawback appears in Q1's statement whatever the refund date | $3,000.00 | $2,000.00 | $10,000.00 |
| B. Clawback in the quarter of the refund, sized by recomputing Q1 with and without the deal ($3,600); Q2 earned goes negative, and the negative amount adds to the recoverable balance | $6,600.00 | −$1,600.00 | $13,600.00 |
| C. As B, but Q2 earned floors at $0 and the excess clawback is forgiven | $6,600.00 | $0.00 | $12,000.00 |

Under A, a quarter already paid out gets rewritten. Under B, a scenario needs the rep's prior-quarter quota and deals so the engine can size the clawback, and the engine computes it rather than being told it.

**Recommended:** Option B. The rep was actually paid the Q1 amount, so the recovery belongs in the period where the refund happened. Rolling any negative amount into the recoverable balance matches your carry-forward answer, and the clawback is still computed by your "recompute without the deal" rule. A refund dated inside the quarter it was booked in behaves the same under A and B.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| A | Clawback always appears in the quarter the deal was booked, regardless of refund date. |
| B | Clawback appears in the quarter containing the refund date, computed from the booking quarter's data; a negative earned commission adds to the recoverable balance. |
| C | As B, but earned commission floors at $0 and the excess clawback is forgiven. |

Numbering is fixed. Starting clarify run 3, question 1:

---

**Question:** When a split deal's shares don't round to whole cents, how is the leftover cent assigned so the shares add back up to the deal amount? (FR-012, FR-018)

**Why it matters:** rounding each share on its own can create or lose a cent. FR-012 promises that credit across reps sums to the deal amount, and a cent in credit can move a tier line.

**Worked scenario:** a $10.01 deal is split 50% / 50% between reps A and B. Each exact share is $5.005.

| Reading | Rep A | Rep B | Sum |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Round each share on its own (half away from zero) | $5.01 | $5.01 | **$10.02**: one cent of credit that was never booked |
| B. Round each share, then give the difference to the rep with the largest split (ties go to the first-listed rep) | $5.01 | $5.00 | **$10.01** |
| C. Round down every share, then hand out the leftover cents one at a time, largest fractional remainder first (ties to the first-listed rep) | $5.01 | $5.00 | **$10.01** |

B and C differ with three or more reps. Take $100.00 split 33.335% / 33.335% / 33.33%, which gives exact shares of $33.335, $33.335 and $33.33.
- **B:** rounding gives $33.34 + $33.34 + $33.33 = $100.01, so the first-listed rep's share drops to $33.33. Result: **$33.33 / $33.34 / $33.33**.
- **C:** rounding down gives $33.33 × 3 = $99.99, and the single leftover cent goes to the largest remainder, the first-listed rep. Result: **$33.34 / $33.33 / $33.33**.

**Recommended:** Option C, the largest-remainder method. It's the standard way to split money exactly: every share is within a cent of its exact value, credit always sums to the deal, and the same rule works for any number of reps. The same allocation applies when a partial refund is split across reps (FR-017).

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| A | Round each share independently; the shares may not sum to the deal amount. |
| B | Round each share; put any difference on the rep with the largest split percentage (ties to the first-listed rep). |
| C | Largest remainder: round every share down to the cent, then give leftover cents one at a time to the shares with the largest fractional remainders (ties to the first-listed rep). |

## STOP: Stages 1–2 (specify and clarify) are ready for your approval

**Elapsed:** stage 1 (specify) ran 21:52:23Z → about 22:00Z. Stage 2 (clarify) ran from about 22:00Z to 22:35:48Z. Together that's about 43 minutes, most of it spent waiting on answers.

**Spec:** [specs/001-commission-calculator/spec.md](specs/001-commission-calculator/spec.md), on branch `001-commission-calculator`. Nothing is committed yet.
- The **Input** field holds the brief verbatim, everything above PROCESS.
- It has 6 user stories: tiers, which date counts, proration, splits, draw, and clawback. There are 31 acceptance scenarios, and every amount in them is tagged `(requirement)`. Each gets an exact-to-the-cent test under Principle II.
- FR-001 to FR-021 and SC-001 to SC-005.

**Clarify:** 21 questions over 6 runs. Each question came with a dollar example, the options and my recommendation. Your answers are recorded verbatim, followed by the option each one selected. Three more scan runs followed:
- Two found only wording defects in text I'd written, each already settled by one of your answers. I fixed those.
- The final run found nothing that changes a payout or an accept/reject outcome.

A fresh-context agent that saw only spec.md did the scans from run 4 onward. It recomputed every stated amount with exact decimal arithmetic, and all of them match.

**Your decisions, in short:**
- **Tiers and dates:** marginal tiers. The booking date decides the quarter. Proration is by calendar days.
- **Splits:** credit is the split share only. Shares are allocated by largest remainder.
- **Draw:** $4,000 a month, with the start month prorated by days. An unrecovered draw carries forward, and the amount payable is never negative.
- **Refunds:**
  - The clawback is the booking quarter recomputed without the refunded revenue, and it appears in the quarter of the refund.
  - Partial and multiple refunds are applied in date order across deals, and a split deal is re-split after each one.
  - A clawback may be negative.
- **Rounding:** each amount is rounded to the cent as it's produced, half away from zero.
- **Bad data:** all malformed or inconsistent input rejects the scenario.

**Decisions I made that you may want to revisit, since none changes any amount paid:**
- **The exact 100% and 150% edges:** under marginal tiers, which band owns the edge only decides which line a slice appears on.
- **Two refunds on the same date:** I ordered them by the deal's position in the list. The order only moves cents between two clawback lines, never their total.
- **Two validations I added:** the quarter must be three whole calendar months, and a refund can't be dated before its booking date.
- **One clawback line per refund:** FR-003's "every amount on its own line" requires it.

**Known finding for analyze:** some secondary numbers aren't tagged yet, such as "$0.00" results and dates. The spec addendum's rule that every number is tagged will flag them, and the remediate loop will fix them.

**Needs your approval:**
- The spec, to go on to `/speckit-plan`.
- Whether to commit the spec to the feature branch now. Per step 5, the planning artifacts reach main together as one PR after analyze, so I'd hold the push and PR until then.

## STOP: Stage 3 (plan) is ready for your approval

**Elapsed:** 22:37:18Z → 22:43:27Z, about 6 minutes by the shell clock.

**Artifacts** (uncommitted, on `001-commission-calculator`): [plan.md](specs/001-commission-calculator/plan.md), [research.md](specs/001-commission-calculator/research.md), [data-model.md](specs/001-commission-calculator/data-model.md), the contracts for the [engine API](specs/001-commission-calculator/contracts/engine-api.md), the [scenario file](specs/001-commission-calculator/contracts/scenario-file.md) and the [UI](specs/001-commission-calculator/contracts/ui.md), and [quickstart.md](specs/001-commission-calculator/quickstart.md).

**Design:**
- **Engine:** a pure `CommissionCalculator.Engine` library with no packages, no I/O and no clock. Money is `decimal`. Each FR is its own small component, marked `[Implements("FR-0xx")]`.
- **Web app:** a Razor Pages app that's only a view. It reads seeded JSON files from its `Scenarios/` folder and renders the engine's lines, with no client script.
- **Tests:**
  - xUnit v3 unit tests.
  - Reqnroll Gherkin features that mirror every acceptance scenario, to the cent.
  - Web tests using WebApplicationFactory with AngleSharp, for structure and FR citations.
- **Traceability:** `tools/Traceability.cs` builds traceability.md from the TRX files, reflection and spec.md.
- **CI:** GitHub Actions. Warnings are errors, `--fail-skips on`, coverage is reported with an 80% floor on the engine, each integration test also runs on its own, plus a smoke run of the app.

**Constitution Check:** passes, including both standing gates. Accessibility has one recorded limitation: there's no automated contrast or axe scan, because that needs a browser in CI. Contrast will be checked by hand.

**The spikes changed three things:**
1. **The usual xUnit/coverlet VSTest setup doesn't run.** On the .NET 10 SDK, `dotnet test` rejects it with xunit.v3 4.x. The fix is opting in to Microsoft.Testing.Platform, which also means switching to MTP's coverage extension.
2. **Skipped tests pass silently.** A skipped test reports "Passed!". `--fail-skips on` was seen turning that into a failure (exit code 2), so CI uses it.
3. **`dotnet run` at the repo root fails** once a solution file is there.

Reqnroll is maintained (last commit 2026-08-26, release v3.3.4 on 2026-03-23). Its xUnit v3 plugin targets xunit 2.x, but the spike showed it works with 4.0.1.

**Decisions for you:**
1. **SC-001 can't be met as written.** It requires every line of every seeded rep's statement to match a value stated in the spec, but the examples state only the amounts they're about.
   - **Option A (recommended):** I add a spec appendix giving the full expected statement for each seeded scenario. I'd compute it by hand from the FRs, independently of the engine, and you'd approve it.
   - **Option B:** narrow SC-001 to "every amount the spec states matches".
2. **How "runs with `dotnet run`" is met.** I'd use `dotnet run --project src/CommissionCalculator.Web` from the root, or plain `dotnet run` inside that folder. Is that acceptable?
3. **For your information, no payout impact:** an earlier-quarter deal listed in both the scenario and its booking-quarter data must be identical in both, or the scenario is rejected. This follows from your "reject inconsistent data" answer.

**Other notes:**
- Only two claims in research.md are still assumptions: that the CI runner resolves SDK 10.0.4xx, and the CI time of the per-test loop. The first CI run settles both.
- The kit's `install.sh --check` can't run in the public repo's CI because the library is private. It stays a local step.
- Leak check: 0 hits outside installer output. No home paths or emails appear in the artifacts.

```
2	from decimal import Decimal as D, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_FLOOR

6	C = D("0.01")
7	def R(x): return x.quantize(C, ROUND_HALF_UP)  # half away from zero for Decimal
8	def days(a, b): return (b - a).days + 1
9	
10	def split(amount, splits):  # FR-012 largest remainder
11	    ex = [amount * D(str(p)) / 100 for _, p in splits]
12	    fl = [e.quantize(C, ROUND_FLOOR) for e in ex]
13	    left = int((amount - sum(fl)) / C)
14	    order = sorted(range(len(splits)), key=lambda i: (-(ex[i] - fl[i]), i))
15	    for i in order[:left]: fl[i] += C
16	    return {splits[i][0]: fl[i] for i in range(len(splits))}

18	def prorated(quota, start, q):  # FR-010
19	    qs, qe = q
20	    if start <= qs: return D(quota)
21	    return R(D(quota) * days(start, qe) / days(qs, qe))

23	def credit_lines(rep, q, deals, applied):
24	    lines = []
25	    for d in deals:

27	        if rep not in [s[0] for s in d["splits"]]: continue
28	        reduced = D(d["amount"]) - sum((D(r["amount"]) for r in applied if r["deal"] == d["id"]), D(0))
29	        lines.append((d, split(reduced, d["splits"])[rep]))

33	    pq = prorated(quota, start, q)
34	    credit = sum((s for _, s in credit_lines(rep, q, deals, applied)), D(0))
35	    e100, e150 = pq, R(D("1.5") * pq)
36	    tiers = []
37	    s1 = min(credit, e100); s2 = min(max(credit - e100, D(0)), e150 - e100); s3 = max(credit - e150, D(0))
38	    for rate, sl in ((D("0.05"), s1), (D("0.08"), s2), (D("0.12"), s3)):
39	        if sl > 0: tiers.append((rate, sl, R(rate * sl)))
40	    return pq, credit, tiers, sum((t[2] for t in tiers), D(0))
```

```
1	# Data Model: Quarterly Sales Commission Calculator
2	
3	All money is an exact decimal in USD with at most two decimal places on input (FR-004). Dates are
4	calendar dates with no time or time zone. Percentages are exact decimals (e.g. `33.335`).
5	
6	## Input entities (engine inputs, read from a scenario file)
7	
8	### Scenario
9	| Field | Type | Rules |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| `id` | string | Unique across seeded scenarios, else a load error naming it (FR-004); used in the page URL. |
12	| `name`, `description` | string | Shown in the picker and page heading. |
13	| `quarter` | Quarter | Must be three whole calendar months starting on the 1st (Edge Cases). |
14	| `roster` | Rep[] | Reps who receive a statement. At least one; unique `repId` (FR-004). |
15	| `deals` | Deal[] | The scenario's own deal list, in listed order (FR-008 lists excluded ones). |
16	| `bookingQuarters` | BookingQuarter[] | Earlier quarters needed to size clawbacks (FR-016). May be empty. |
17	
18	### Quarter
19	| Field | Type | Rules |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| `start`, `end` | date | `start` is the 1st of a month; `end` is the last day of the third month. |
22	
23	Derived: `Days = end − start + 1`; `Months` = the three calendar months.
24	
25	### Rep
26	| Field | Type | Rules |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| `repId`, `name` | string | |
29	| `quota` | money | > 0, whole cents (FR-004, FR-005). |
30	| `startDate` | date | On or before `quarter.end` (FR-011). |
31	| `openingRecoverableBalance` | money | ≥ 0, whole cents, default 0.00 (FR-004, FR-015). |
32	
33	### Deal
34	| Field | Type | Rules |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| `dealId` | string | Unique within its quarter's deal list (FR-004). |
37	| `amount` | money | > 0, whole cents. |
38	| `closeDate` | date | Informational only (FR-008). |
39	| `bookingDate` | date | Decides the quarter (FR-008). |
40	| `splits` | SplitCredit[] | ≥ 1; percentages sum to exactly 100 (FR-013); each rep at most once (FR-004); every rep's start date ≤ `bookingDate` (FR-011). |
41	| `refunds` | Refund[] | In listed order; total ≤ `amount` (FR-017). |
42	
43	### SplitCredit
44	| Field | Type | Rules |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| `repId` | string | For the scenario's own deals: on the roster (FR-004). For booking-quarter deals: on the roster or in that quarter's `partners`. |
47	| `percent` | decimal | > 0 and ≤ 100 (FR-004). |
48	
49	### Refund
50	| Field | Type | Rules |
51	|---|---|---|
52	| `amount` | money | > 0, whole cents. |
53	| `date` | date | ≥ the deal's `bookingDate`
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Writes a CI-evidence record for a CI gate (not a test): tasks T035, maintainer decision D1.
# Arguments: <job> <check> <requirement-ids, comma-separated> <outcome>
set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p ci-evidence
job="$1"; check="$2"; requirements="$3"; outcome="$4"
ids="$(printf '%s' "$requirements" | sed 's/[^,][^,]*/"&"/g')"
cat > "ci-evidence/$job.json" <<JSON
{
  "job": "$job",
  "check": "$check",
  "requirements": [$ids],
  "result": "$outcome",
  "commit": "${GITHUB_SHA:-local}",
  "runUrl": "${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}"
}
JSON
cat "ci-evidence/$job.json"
engine-79.cobertura.xml
engine-85.cobertura.xml
merge-a.cobertura.xml
merge-b.cobertura.xml
no-engine.cobertura.xml
two-tests.trx
```

```
on:
  pull_request:

    branches: [main]

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
      - name: Build (warnings are errors)
        run: dotnet build CommissionCalculator.slnx -warnaserror
      - name: Test (skips fail the run)
        run: dotnet test --solution CommissionCalculator.slnx --no-build --fail-skips on --report-trx --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura
      - name: Engine coverage floor
        run: tools/ci/coverage-gate.sh 80 | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: Each test alone
        run: tools/ci/isolated-tests.sh
      - name: Upload test results and coverage
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: test-results
          path: TestResults/

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
      - name: Evidence of a clean tree (no bin/ or obj/)
        run: git status --ignored --short
      - name: Start with one command and serve the page
        id: smoke
        run: tools/ci/smoke.sh '/?scenario=tiers' Avery
      - name: Record CI evidence (SC-004, FR-020)
        if: always()
        run: tools/ci/evidence.sh smoke "clean checkout starts with one command and serves /" "SC-004,FR-020" "${{ steps.smoke.outcome }}"
      - name: Upload CI evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ci-evidence-smoke
          path: ci-evidence/

  offline-smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
      - name: Serve the published app with no network

      - name: Record CI evidence (SC-004)

        run: tools/ci/evidence.sh offline-smoke "published app serves / with no network" "SC-004" "${{ steps.offline.outcome }}"
```

```
using System.Globalization;
using System.Reflection;
using CommissionCalculator.Tools;

switch (args)
{
    case ["coverage-gate", var floor, var engineAssembly, .. var reports] when reports.Length > 0:
        var result = CoverageGate.Evaluate(
            reports.Select(File.ReadAllText).ToList(),
            engineHasTypes: Assembly.LoadFrom(engineAssembly).GetTypes().Length > 0,
            floorPercent: decimal.Parse(floor, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));
        Console.WriteLine(result.Message);
        return result.Passed ? 0 : 1;

    case ["list-tests", var trx]:
        foreach (var test in TrxTestList.List(File.ReadAllText(trx)))
        {
            Console.WriteLine(test);
        }

        return 0;

    case ["trace", .. var options]:
        return Trace.Run(options);

    default:
        Console.Error.WriteLine("usage: coverage-gate <floor-percent> <engine.dll> <cobertura.xml>...");
        Console.Error.WriteLine("       list-tests <results.trx>");
        Console.Error.WriteLine("       trace [--spec <spec.md>] --assemblies <dll>... --results <trx>... "
            + "[--evidence <json>...] [--out <traceability.md>] [--strict]");
        return 2;
}
```

```
import subprocess, sys, shutil, re, os
def run(file, find, replace, project, label):
    orig=open(file).read()
    assert orig.count(find)==1, (label, find[:50])
    shutil.copy(file, file+'.bak')
    open(file,'w').write(orig.replace(find, replace))
    try:
        b=subprocess.run(['dotnet','build',project,'-v','q'],capture_output=True,text=True)
        if b.returncode!=0:
            print(f"{label}: BUILD FAILED (guard not applicable as written)"); return
        r=subprocess.run(['dotnet','test','--project',project,'--no-build'],capture_output=True,text=True)
        failed=sorted(set(re.sub(r' \(.*','',l[7:]) for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith('failed ')))
        tot=re.search(r'failed: (\d+)', r.stdout)
        print(f"{label}: failed={tot.group(1) if tot else '?'} -> {[f.split('.')[-1] for f in failed][:6]}")
    finally:
        shutil.move(file+'.bak', file)
        os.utime(file, None)  # newer than the guard build, so incremental builds recompile it
```

````
# Quickstart & validation: Quarterly Sales Commission Calculator

## Prerequisites

.NET SDK 10.0.4xx (`global.json` pins 10.0.400, rolling forward to later 10.0 feature bands).
No other services, accounts or network access at run time.

## Run

```bash
dotnet run --project src/CommissionCalculator.Web
```

(or `dotnet run` from inside `src/CommissionCalculator.Web`), then open the URL it prints.

## Test

```bash
dotnet build -warnaserror
dotnet test --fail-skips on --report-trx --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura
dotnet run --project tools/CommissionCalculator.Tools -- trace \
  --assemblies src/CommissionCalculator.Engine/bin/Debug/net10.0/CommissionCalculator.Engine.dll \
               src/CommissionCalculator.Web/bin/Debug/net10.0/CommissionCalculator.Web.dll \
  --results $(find . \( -name '*.trx' -path '*TestResults*' \) -o -path '*ci-evidence/*.json')
```

## Validation steps (each falsifiable)

1. **Fresh clone runs (SC-004).** Condition: a clean clone — evidence: `git status --ignored` shows
   no `bin/`/`obj/` immediately before running. Run the command above; expect `/` to return HTTP
   200 and the picker to list every file in `Scenarios/`. CI repeats this from a fresh checkout and
   additionally requests `/?scenario=tiers` (tasks T010, T060b).
2. **No network at run time (SC-004).** Condition: no network — evidence: `docker inspect` shows
   `NetworkMode: none` immediately before the request. CI's offline-smoke job runs the published app
   in `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0.12` with `--network none` and requests `/` (T035) and
   `/?scenario=tiers` (T060b) from a curl container sharing that network namespace; expect a rep
   table, and expect the same sidecar's request to an external host to fail. The result is a
   CI-evidence record, not a test (traceability "Verified by CI job").
3. **Every seeded amount matches the spec (SC-001).** Run the test command; expect the
   `SeededScenarios.feature` scenarios to pass and zero skipped (the run fails on any skip).
4. **Every line cites an FR (FR-003, SC-002).** Web tests assert every breakdown row's Rule cell is
   an FR ID present in spec.md; the traceability report's "Unexplained" gaps are empty.
5. **Rejected scenario (FR-004).** Select "Invalid data (rejected)"; expect an alert listing each
   error with its FR, and no rep tables (asserted by T048).
6. **Keyboard only (SC-005, FR-021).** Condition: no pointer input — evidence: the check is driven
   through the in-app browse
````

```
namespace CommissionCalculator.Web.Catalog;

public sealed class ScenarioOptions
{
    // The build/publish output, not the content root: a seed file missing from output is missing
    // at run time, which is what the smoke checks need to see (tasks T024).
    public string Directory { get; set; } = Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "Scenarios");
}

[Engine.Implements("FR-001")]
public sealed class ScenarioCatalog
{
    public ScenarioCatalog(string directory)
    {
        if (!System.IO.Directory.Exists(directory))
        {
            return;
        }

        var results = System.IO.Directory.GetFiles(directory, "*.json")
            .Order(StringComparer.Ordinal)
            .Select(path => ScenarioFileReader.Read(Path.GetFileName(path), File.ReadAllText(path)))
            .ToList();

        var read = results.OfType<ScenarioRead>().Select(result => result.File).ToList();
        var duplicateIds = read.GroupBy(file => file.Scenario.Id)
            .Where(group => group.Count() > 1)
            .ToDictionary(group => group.Key, group => group.Select(file => file.FileName).ToList());

        Scenarios = read.Where(file => !duplicateIds.ContainsKey(file.Scenario.Id)).ToList();
        LoadErrors = results.OfType<ScenarioReadFailed>().Select(result => result.Error)
            .Concat(read.Where(file => duplicateIds.ContainsKey(file.Scenario.Id))
                .Select(file => new ScenarioLoadError(file.FileName,
                    $"Scenario id '{file.Scenario.Id}' is declared by more than one file: {string.Join(", ", duplicateIds[file.Scenario.Id])}.")))
            .OrderBy(error => error.FileName, StringComparer.Ordinal)
            .ToList();
    }

    public IReadOnlyList<ScenarioFile> Scenarios { get; } = [];

    public IReadOnlyList<ScenarioLoadError> LoadErrors { get; } = [];
}
```

```
using System.Globalization;

namespace CommissionCalculator.Web.Presentation;

public static class Format
{
    private const string MinusSign = "−";

    // A negative amount carries a minus sign in its text, never colour alone (FR-021).
    [Engine.Implements("FR-021")]
    public static string Money(decimal amount) =>
        (amount < 0m ? MinusSign : "") + "$" + Math.Abs(amount).ToString("#,##0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);

    // Two decimals, half away from zero; display only (FR-002).
    [Engine.Implements("FR-002")]
    public static string Attainment(decimal ratio) =>
        Math.Round(ratio * 100m, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero).ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) + "%";
}
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs every test of the last suite run on its own, so a test that only passes because another
# test ran first fails here (constitution Principle II: each test passes alone).
set -euo pipefail
failed=0
for trx in TestResults/*.trx; do
  project_name="$(basename "$trx" | sed -E 's/_net[0-9.]+_[a-z0-9]+\.trx$//')"
  project="$(find tests -name "$project_name.csproj" | head -1)"
  [ -n "$project" ] || { echo "no project for $trx" >&2; exit 1; }
  while IFS= read -r test; do
    if dotnet test --project "$project" --no-build --fail-skips on --filter-method "$test" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "alone ok   $test"
    else
      echo "alone FAIL $test"; failed=1
    fi
  done < <(dotnet run --project tools/CommissionCalculator.Tools --no-build -- list-tests "$trx")
done
exit "$failed"
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: leakcheck.sh <dir> [git-rev-range-for-messages]
S=$(dirname "$0"); DIR="$1"; RANGE="${2:-}"; total=0; inst=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r doc phrase; do
  hits=$(grep -rlF --exclude-dir=.git -- "$phrase" "$DIR" 2>/dev/null)
  msg=0; [ -n "$RANGE" ] && msg=$(git -C "$DIR" log --format=%B $RANGE 2>/dev/null | grep -cF -- "$phrase")
  for f in $hits; do rel=${f#$DIR/}
    case "$rel" in .specify/*|.claude/*) echo "  INSTALLER-OUTPUT HIT [$doc] $rel"; inst=$((inst+1));;
      *) echo "  HIT [$doc] $rel"; total=$((total+1));; esac; done
  [ "$msg" != 0 ] && { echo "  HIT [$doc] in commit messages"; total=$((total+1)); }
done < "$S/phrases.tsv"
echo "non-installer hits: $total; installer-output hits: $inst; phrases: $(wc -l < $S/phrases.tsv)"
```

````
# Commission Calculator

A local web app that computes quarterly sales commission for a SaaS sales team from seeded
scenarios, and shows every rep's statement line by line, each line citing the requirement (FR)
that produced it.

The requirements, decisions and expected amounts live in
[`specs/001-commission-calculator/spec.md`](specs/001-commission-calculator/spec.md); Appendix A
holds the full expected statement for every seeded scenario.

## Run

Requires the .NET 10 SDK (`global.json` pins 10.0.400 and rolls forward within 10.0).

```bash
dotnet run --project src/CommissionCalculator.Web
```

or, from inside `src/CommissionCalculator.Web`, plain `dotnet run`. Then open the URL it prints.

Scenarios are read from the `Scenarios` folder next to the built app. To read them from somewhere
else, pass the optional setting `Scenarios:Directory` (added with the scenario catalog in
implementation Phase 2):

```bash
dotnet run --project src/CommissionCalculator.Web -- --Scenarios:Directory=/path/to/scenarios
```

## Test

```bash
dotnet build CommissionCalculator.slnx -warnaserror
dotnet test --solution CommissionCalculator.slnx --fail-skips on --report-trx --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura
tools/ci/coverage-gate.sh 80
tools/ci/isolated-tests.sh
```

Skipped tests fail the run, the engine's line coverage must be at least 80%, and every test must
also pass when run on its own. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the same steps, plus a smoke
job that starts the app from a clean checkout.

## Layout

- `src/CommissionCalculator.Engine` — the commission rules; no I/O, no clock, exact `decimal` money.
- `src/CommissionCalculator.Web` — Razor Pages view of the engine's statements.
- `tests/` — unit tests (xUnit v3) and Gherkin feature files (Reqnroll) mirroring the spec's
  acceptance scenarios.
- `tools/` — CI helpers (coverage gate, test lister) and, later, the traceability generator.
````

## Findings

### 1. An earlier-quarter deal listed in both the scenario's deal list and booking-quarter data is always falsely rejected — entire statement suppressed

**Input** (JSON as fed to `CommissionEngine.Calculate`; the two `E1` entries are byte-for-byte identical):

```json
{"id":"dup","quarter":["2026-04-01","2026-06-30"],
 "roster":[{"repId":"r1","quota":"100000.00","start":"2025-06-01","opening":"0"}],
 "deals":[
   {"dealId":"Q2D","amount":"40000.00","close":"2026-05-01","book":"2026-05-04","splits":[["r1","100"]],"refunds":[]},
   {"dealId":"E1","amount":"60000.00","close":"2026-01-09","book":"2026-01-10","splits":[["r1","100"]],"refunds":[["60000.00","2026-04-15"]]}],
 "bookingQuarters":[{"quarter":["2026-01-01","2026-03-31"],
   "reps":[{"repId":"r1","quota":"100000.00","start":"2025-06-01"}],"partners":[],
   "deals":[
     {"dealId":"E1","amount":"60000.00","close":"2026-01-09","book":"2026-01-10","splits":[["r1","100"]],"refunds":[["60000.00","2026-04-15"]]},
     {"dealId":"E2","amount":"60000.00","close":"2026-02-09","book":"2026-02-10","splits":[["r1","100"]],"refunds":[]}]}]}
```

**Spec contradicted** — FR-004 rejects only when they *differ*: "or an earlier-quarter deal listed both in the scenario's own deal list and in booking-quarter data **differs between the two**". Here they do not differ. FR-004 also requires a rejected scenario to "MUST NOT show any payout", so a false rejection suppresses the whole statement.

**Expected** (derived twice; the second derivation is Appendix A.10 Sage, which is the identical shape): Q1 commission before refunds = 5% × $100,000.00 = $5,000.00 plus 8% × $20,000.00 = $1,600.00 → $6,600.00; with E1 removed, bookings $60,000.00 → 5% = $3,000.00; clawback = $6,600.00 − $3,000.00 = **$3,600.00**. Q2: credited bookings $40,000.00, 5% = $2,000.00; earned = $2,000.00 − $3,600.00 = **−$1,600.00**; draws $12,000.00; recovered $0.00; payable $0.00; closing recoverable balance **$13,600.00**. Plus an excluded-deal line for E1 at $0.00 (FR-008).

**Actual**: `RejectedScenario` — `[FR-004] "Deal 'E1' differs between the two lists."` No statement, no payout.

**Root cause, established black-box**: I passed the *same* `DealInput` object instance into both lists → accepted, and the engine then produced exactly the expected statement above. Structurally identical but separately constructed instances → rejected. Sharing only `Splits` → still rejected; only `Refunds` → still rejected; sharing both → accepted. That is C# positional-record equality, whose `IReadOnlyList&lt;SplitCredit&gt;`/`IReadOnlyList&lt;RefundInput&gt;` members compare by *reference*. Any real loader (JSON, file, DB) constructs separate lists, so the check can never pass.

It also fires on refund-free duplicates: adding the identical `E2` to the scenario's own deal list yields two errors, `"Deal 'E1' differs…"` and `"Deal 'E2' differs…"`. This matters because FR-004's precondition requires booking-quarter data to include *every* deal the rep booked that quarter, while the app also lists earlier-quarter deals as excluded (Appendix A.2 B-4) — so the overlap is the natural data shape.

**Dollar impact**: the full statement (here a $3,600.00 clawback and a $13,600.00 closing balance); unbounded in general. **Confidence: high.**

### 2. Spurious rejection reason: "refunds total more than the deal amount" on a deal with no refunds

**Input**: `{"dealId":"X","amount":"-100.00","close":"2026-01-05","book":"2026-01-06","splits":[["r1","100"]],"refunds":[]}` in a Q1-2026 scenario.

**Spec contradicted** — FR-004: "A scenario that violates a validation rule … MUST be shown as rejected **with the reasons**"; the rule cited is the Edge Case "A refund of zero or less, or refunds on one deal totalling more than the deal amount, are rejected." There are no refunds; their total is $0.00.

**Expected**: one error — `"Deal 'X': amount must be greater than zero."`
**Actual**: that error **plus** `[FR-004] "Deal 'X': refunds total more than the deal amount."` The guard is evidently `sum(refunds) &gt; amount`, and `0 &gt; −100` is true.

Positive control: a deal of `"0.00"` with no refunds produces only the amount error, so the message is emitted exactly when the amount is negative.

**Dollar impact: $0.00** (the scenario is correctly rejected either way) — it is a wrong reason, not a wrong payout. **Confidence: high.**

## Areas probed hard with no finding

All of the following were checked against the reference to the cent, line for line, including FR IDs and line ordering. Every one is clean.

- **Appendix A**, all 10 calculated scenarios and the rejected one — exact match (this is the positive control for both the engine and my reference).
- **Tier boundaries**: bookings at exactly 100%, 100% ± $0.01, exactly 150%, 150% ± $0.01; quotas with odd cents so the 150% edge lands on a half-cent; quotas of $0.01/$0.03 against $500,000 bookings; half-cent tier-line rounding at 5%, 8%, 12%; zero bookings (no tier lines).
- **The rounded 150% band edge** (FR-018) is genuinely exercised: I searched for inputs where the rounded-edge and unrounded-edge readings differ by a cent, found 2,720 in a small sweep, and ran five realistic ones (e.g. quota $17,394.27, bookings $26,092.95 → $1,565.66 rounded-edge vs $1,565.67 unrounded). The engine follows the rounded edge, as FR-018 explicitly requires.
- **Proration**: start on the quarter's first day, second day, last day; start dates producing half-cent prorated quotas; prorated quota rounding to $0.00 (correctly rejected) and to $0.01; a mid-quarter starter whose prorated quota rounds back to the full quota (the FR-010 line is still emitted — correct).
- **Quarter shapes**: 89/90/91/92-day quarters, leap Q1 2024, a quarter ending on 2024-02-29, and non-calendar-aligned quarters (2025-11-01..2026-01-31, 2026-02-01..2026-04-30).
- **Draws**: start on a month's last day, on a month's first day, on the quarter's last day, on 2024-02-29; half-cent draw rounding.
- **Splits**: $0.01 split 50/50 (tie → first-listed rep) and reversed; 99/1 and 1/99; three-way thirds; seven-way 24-decimal percentages; a four-way tie for two leftover cents; $999,999.99 at 70/30.
- **Refunds**: full, repeated partial, partials totalling exactly the deal; two deals refunded on the same date (and with the deal list reversed); two refunds on one deal on the same date; refunds on the quarter's first and last day and the day after; a refund crossing a tier boundary; one-cent and sub-half-cent refunds; negative clawbacks from re-splits; re-split lines present for split deals and absent for solo deals and for out-of-quarter refunds.
- **Earlier-quarter refunds**: prorated booking-quarter quota; booking-quarter quota differing from this quarter's; two booking quarters in one statement; off-roster split partners participating in the re-split; earlier refunds dated inside the booking quarter applied before sizing the current one; refunds listed out of date order; cross-deal ordering by refund date.
- **Draw recovery**: earned above/below/equal to the recoverable total; opening balances including $0.01; earned exactly $0.00; negative earned with and without an opening balance.
- **Validation**: 43 targeted probes — duplicate repId/dealId (roster, own list, booking-quarter list), rep twice on one deal, empty roster, 0%/&gt;100%/negative split percentages, sums of 99.99%/100.01%, zero/negative/non-cent quotas, deal amounts, refunds and opening balances, refund before booking date, refunds exceeding (and exactly equalling) the deal, quarters of 2/4 months, not starting on the 1st, reversed, one day short, off-roster credit on counted *and* excluded deals, start after quarter end, start on the last day, deal booked before/on a rep's start date (counted and excluded), missing booking-quarter data, overlapping booking quarter, booking quarter not three months, booking-quarter deal booked outside its own dates, booking-quarter start date differing from the roster, missing booking-quarter rep entry, partner with no start date, FR-011 against a partner, and a multi-error scenario. All behaved as the spec requires (aside from finding 2).
- **Randomised differential fuzzing**: 2,800 general scenarios (7 seeds) plus 2,000 boundary-biased scenarios (4 seeds) placing bookings a cent either side of the 100% and 150% edges over odd prorated quotas — **zero** numeric mismatches.

One non-finding worth knowing: `RepStatement.Attainment` is the raw ratio (`0.8`, `1.1111…`), not the two-decimal-place percentage FR-002 describes. FR-002 says attainment "is shown as" a percentage and "is display only", so the formatting belongs to the caller — but the engine's public API gives no rounded value, so a UI that prints it directly would violate FR-002.

## Genuine spec ambiguities

**I found none where two readings pay different amounts.** The clarifications close every payout-affecting question I probed — notably the marginal tiers, booking-date crediting, share-only attainment, calendar-day proration, recompute-based clawbacks, largest-remainder splits with ties to the first-listed rep, re-split after each refund, and FR-018's explicit rounding of the 150% band edge.

Two things are genuinely unspecified but carry a **$0.00 differential**:

1. **Order of clawback lines across booking quarters.** FR-017 fixes the order only within one quarter: "For each rep, all refunds on deals booked in **the same quarter** are applied in refund-date order across deals". When a rep has refunds from this quarter *and* an earlier one (or from two earlier ones), the spec does not say how the lines interleave. The engine groups by quarter (own quarter first, then booking quarters in listed order); a global refund-date order is an equally valid reading. Each clawback is recomputed inside its own quarter, so no amount changes — differential **$0.00**. My reference initially used the date-ordered reading and produced 34 line-order diffs across 400 fuzz cases with every amount identical.

2. **Whether a re-split line is shown for a refund dated outside the scenario's quarter.** The 2026-09-21 analyze clarification says "after each refund on a split deal, the rep's statement shows a line with their re-split share", while FR-016 says "A refund dated after the scenario's quarter ends has no effect on that quarter's statement". The engine shows the re-split line only alongside an in-quarter clawback, consistent with Appendix A.9. Presentation only — differential **$0.00**.

**STOP — step 7 complete.** Elapsed for this stage: ~50 minutes (converge assessment ran while the adversarial subagent worked; the subagent itself took 16 minutes and ~200k tokens).

**PR:** [#13 Converge and adversarial review](https://github.com/gregoryschroeder/commission-calculator-sdlc/pull/13) — all four CI jobs green ([run 35780882474](https://github.com/gregoryschroeder/commission-calculator-sdlc/actions/runs/35780882474)). 236/236 tests, 0 skipped; engine line coverage 98.69%; leak check 0 non-installer hits.

**The adversarial pass found one defect that suppressed real payouts.** FR-004 rejects a deal listed both in the scenario's own deals and in booking-quarter data *only when the two entries differ*. The check used `!=`, and `DealInput`'s compiler-generated equality compares its `Splits` and `Refunds` **lists by reference** — so two entries read from the same JSON are never equal. Every scenario with that overlap was rejected outright and showed no figures at all. That overlap is the natural data shape: FR-004 requires booking-quarter data to hold every deal of that quarter, while FR-008 lists the earlier-quarter deal as excluded on the page.

The seeded scenarios never tripped it, and neither did the existing "differs between them" test — it builds the duplicate with `with { Amount = … }` from the same instance, so the lists were shared references and only the amount differed. A test written from the spec rather than from the code is exactly what caught it.

Both fixes went test-first and watched failing: the unit test rebuilds the deal with fresh split and refund objects, and the integration scenario failed with `Expected: CalculatedScenario, Actual: RejectedScenario`. It now pays the AS2 figures — $3,600.00 clawback, −$1,600.00 earned, $13,600.00 closing balance — which I derived independently before the fix. The second defect (a refund-free deal accused of "refunds total more than the deal amount", because `0 > -100`) costs nothing but showed a wrong reason. Guards confirm both rules still fail when their behaviour is removed.

**Two things I deliberately did not change**, and one needs your call:

1. `RepStatement.Attainment` is the raw ratio, not a rounded percentage — correct, since FR-002 makes attainment display-only and the web rounds it; rounding in the engine would put presentation in the domain.
2. Two spec silences, each with a **$0.00** differential, so I'm flagging rather than deciding: FR-017 fixes clawback order only *within* one booking quarter, leaving the order across two quarters unstated (the engine groups by quarter, own quarter first); and whether a re-split line shows for a refund dated outside the quarter (the engine follows Appendix A.9). Both are line-order, not payout. Say the word if you want either written into the spec.

The pass found nothing else: Appendix A in full, tier and proration boundaries, leap quarters, splits to the cent, refund sequencing, draw recovery, 43 validation probes and 4,800 randomised differential scenarios, zero numeric mismatches.

Next, on your approval to merge #13: step 8, the traceability document — which is already generated and committed; I'd re-run the generator against the merged state and confirm it, then STOP. After that, the transcript step.

- **IDs with no test (3):** FR-019, SC-004, SC-005.

Every one of those is still listed as a gap — that was the design decision at T061, because a gap that disappears when you explain it is not traceability — but each carries its category and reason: FR-019 is out of scope (USD only, no tax/FX/multi-year, so nothing implements it); SC-001–SC-003 are evidence-only criteria proved by the seeded-scenario and page tests rather than by any single member; SC-004 is verified by the smoke and offline-smoke CI jobs, whose records appear under "Verified by CI job" with their result and run URL and are never counted as tests; SC-005 is your manual keyboard and VoiceOver checks, with the PRs where they were recorded. A failed CI record would push SC-004 back to Unexplained — that behaviour has its own test.

The report also lists the **18 tooling tests** separately, by the principle they enforce, so they never stand in for coverage of a requirement.

The `traceability` CI job runs the same generator with `--strict` over the other jobs' artifacts, so a future change that leaves an FR without a test or a member fails the build rather than quietly producing a worse report.

That closes stages 0–8. The remaining item is the transcript step: redacted `.jsonl` plus a Markdown rendering under `transcript/`, with the leak proofs run before committing. Say the word and I'll start it.
